LESSON: WOODWORK ING JOINTS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: WOODWORK
Strand: Wood Processes and Products
Topic 3.2: Woodwork ing joints
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 26

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Woodwork ing joints, part of Wood Processes and Products in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 WOODWORK.

Key inquiry question: How are wood joints constructed? 2. Why are wood fasteners important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss different types of joints in wood work, Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech as they are lip read by peers, learner support assistant or teacher. They could also sign, use total communication or write on different types of joints in woodwork,

2. discuss in purposive groups classification of wood joints (lengthening, widening and framing),

3. sketch woodworking joints (lengthening, widening and framing), Learners with manipulation difficulties could use 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss different types of joints in wood work, Learners with speech difficulties could use residual speech as they are lip read by peers, learner support assistant or teacher. They could also sign, use total communication or write on different types of joints in woodwork,
2. discuss in purposive groups classification of wood joints (lengthening, widening and framing),
3. sketch woodworking joints (lengthening, widening and framing), Learners with manipulation difficulties could use 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Woodwork ing joints together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: learner develops speaking, listening and teamwork skills when discussing

classification of woodworking joints.

● Learning to Learn: learners reflect on their own work when visiting nearby wood workshops to observe the application of

wood joints.

● Digital Literacy: learner develops digital skills when interacting and manipulating digital devices when watching video

clips on how to prepare and assemble different woodworking joints

Values:
● Unity: learner collaborate with others as they construct woodworking joints

30

● Respect: learner appreciate each other’s contribution when discussing classification of woodworking joints

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety and security: learner handles tools to fabricate and strengthen joints.

Suggested learning resources: assorted pieces of wood, adhesives, fasteners, career brochures and magazines, realias.
